<!-- page: help/troubleshooting (md/help/troubleshooting.md) -->
# Troubleshooting

> Solutions for black screens, slow virtual machines, programs that do not start, no sound, no Wi-Fi, full memory and lost files.

Start with the **[self-test](self-test.md)**: it often tells you exactly what is wrong.

## Black screen after the boot menu

1. **Wait two minutes**: a slow USB stick or a VM can take that long the first time.
2. Restart and choose **Workstation (KMS / no nomodeset)** in the [boot menu](../start/boot-menu.md). This uses the graphics card's own driver.
3. In VirtualBox: **Settings → Display → Graphics Controller: VMSVGA**, Video Memory 128 MB, 3D acceleration **off**.
4. Choose **Workstation (verbose / no Plymouth)** to see the messages, or **DEBUG: Text Console** to log in as `user` / `user` and look at the logs: `journalctl -b -p err`.

## The screen resolution is wrong or too small

**Settings → Display**. If the resolution you want is missing, start with **Workstation (KMS / no nomodeset)**. In VirtualBox the window does not resize automatically (no Guest Additions); see [VirtualBox](../start/virtualbox.md#screen-size-copy-and-paste-shared-folders).

## Blender or a renderer does not start

- **"Illegal instruction"**, or Blender closes at once: the processor (or the virtual machine) does not offer **SSE4.2** or **AVX**. Check with `grep -o -w -E 'sse4_2|avx' /proc/cpuinfo | sort -u`. In QEMU add `-cpu host`; in other VMs choose "host CPU" passthrough. On a real computer from before about 2011 these programs cannot run.
- Blender starts but the viewport is black or very slow: in a VM this is normal for EEVEE (software OpenGL). Use **Workbench** or **Cycles** (CPU).
- Start it from a terminal to see the error message: type `blender` and read the last lines.

## Everything is slow

| Where | Fix |
|---|---|
| In a VM | give it more memory (8 GB+) and processors (4+). Close programs on the host. |
| Live session from USB | use a USB 3 stick in a USB 3 port (blue), or install Animux. |
| During rendering | normal: rendering uses every core. Lower the priority: `nice -n 19 blender -b …` |
| Blender viewport | use *Solid* shading while animating; lower *Viewport* subdivision levels. |

Watch what uses the computer: **System → Task Manager** or `htop`.

## Memory is full / programs crash in the live session

In the live session, files you save are kept in memory. Delete old renders, save to a USB drive instead, or install Animux. Check: `free -h` and `df -h /`.

## No sound

1. Click the speaker icon: is it muted? Turn the volume up.
2. **Sound Engineering → Sound Server Configuration → PulseAudio Volume Control** → *Output Devices* and *Configuration*: choose the right device (speakers, HDMI, headphones) and profile.
3. A JACK program (Ardour, Hydrogen) is silent: start it with `pw-jack ardour`.

## No Wi-Fi

- Click the network icon at the top right. Is Wi-Fi enabled? Is the network listed?
- Some Wi-Fi chips need firmware Animux does not have, or are switched off with a key (airplane mode) on the laptop.
- Show the chip: `lspci -nnk | grep -A3 -i network` and search the web for its name plus "Debian 12".
- A USB Wi-Fi stick or a cable (or phone USB tethering) always works.

## A USB stick or disk does not appear

Unplug and plug it in again; look in the file manager's left panel. A Windows disk from a computer with *Fast Startup* may be locked: shut Windows down fully (hold **Shift** while clicking *Shut down*).

## I forgot my password (installed system)

Restart; in the start menu choose **Advanced options → recovery mode**, then **root** and type `passwd your-login-name`. Then `reboot`.

## "No bootable option" after installing (UEFI)

An Animux installed on a **UEFI** computer or VM up to r16 may not start when the disk is moved to another computer or VM, or when the firmware forgets its boot list: the screen says *No bootable option or device was found*. The installer wrote Animux's start file only to `EFI/Animux/`, not to the standard fallback place `EFI/BOOT/BOOTX64.EFI`.

To start it once: open the firmware menu (press a key at that message, or **F2**/**Del** at start-up), choose **Boot Maintenance Manager → Boot From File** (the name differs between makers), then the disk → `EFI` → `Animux` → `grubx64.efi`.

To fix it for good, in Animux open a terminal and type:

```
sudo grub-install --target=x86_64-efi --efi-directory=/boot/efi --removable
```

From then on the disk starts on any UEFI computer. (Tested in VirtualBox with an installed r16. Animux r16.1 (`_25`) and later do this when installing.)

## A program froze

Close it with the × button and wait. If it does not close: **System → Task Manager**, select it, **End Task**; or in a terminal `pkill -f programname`. In Blender, **File → Recover → Auto Save** brings back recent work.

## I lost my files after a restart

In the live session, nothing is kept after a restart. See [The live session](../start/live-session.md). Files deleted in the file manager are in the **Trash** until you empty it.

## The fail2ban service failed

On r16 (`_21`), `fail2ban` shows as failed at start-up (Debian 12 has no `/var/log/auth.log`); it does not affect anything else. Fixed in r16.1: it reads the system journal instead. To fix it on r16, in a [terminal](../desktop/terminal.md):

```
sudo apt install python3-systemd
printf '[sshd]\nbackend = systemd\n' | sudo tee /etc/fail2ban/jail.d/animux.conf
sudo systemctl restart fail2ban
```

(Tested on an installed Animux: afterwards `sudo fail2ban-client status sshd` shows the jail.)

## Still stuck?

See [Getting help](getting-help.md).


---
<!-- page: help/faq (md/help/faq.md) -->
# Questions and answers

> Short answers to the questions new Animux users ask most often.

**Is Animux free? Can I use it for paid work?**
Yes and yes. Animux and its programs are free and open source. Your films, images and models belong to you. See [Licences](../about/licenses.md).

**Do I have to know Linux?**
No. This guide explains everything from the start. You need the terminal for only a few jobs, and the guide gives the full command each time.

**Will Animux delete Windows?**
Not unless you tell the installer to. The live session and virtual machines change nothing. When [installing](../start/install.md), choose *Install alongside* to keep Windows.

**Can I open my Maya / 3ds Max / Cinema 4D / After Effects files?**
Not directly. Export them from the old program as **FBX**, **OBJ**, **USD** or **Alembic** and import them in Blender. Images and videos (PNG, EXR, MP4) work everywhere.

**Does Animux have Photoshop, Toon Boom, Maya or After Effects?**
No, those are commercial programs for Windows and macOS. Animux has free alternatives: Krita/GIMP (painting, photos), Pencil2D/Synfig/Krita (2D animation), Blender (3D, compositing), Kdenlive (editing). DaVinci Resolve can be installed: [Adding software](../desktop/add-software.md#davinci-resolve).

**Which program should I learn first?**
For 2D: [Pencil2D](../software/pencil2d.md), then Krita or Synfig. For 3D: [Blender](../software/blender.md). For editing: Kdenlive. Follow the [tutorials](../tutorials/first-3d-render.md) in order.

**Can Blender render on my graphics card?**
With an NVIDIA card and NVIDIA's driver (CUDA/OptiX) or an AMD card with ROCm (HIP), yes. Without them, Blender renders on the processor, which always works. See [Adding software](../desktop/add-software.md#nvidia-driver).

**Why is Blender 5 and not Debian's Blender 3.4?**
Debian 12's Blender is from 2022. Animux packages the official Blender 5.2 LTS release from blender.org.

**Can I use a drawing tablet?**
Yes. Wacom, Huion, XP-Pen and others work with pressure in Krita, GIMP, MyPaint, Pencil2D and Blender.

**Do my files survive a restart?**
In the live session: **no**. Installed: yes. See [The live session](../start/live-session.md).

**How do I update Animux?**
`sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade` on an installed system. See [Updates](../desktop/add-software.md#updates).

**Can several computers render together?**
Yes, with [Flamenco](../software/flamenco.md).

**Does Animux run on a Mac?**
On Intel Macs in VirtualBox, VMware Fusion or Parallels, and from USB on many models. On Apple Silicon (M1–M4) only through very slow emulation.

**Is Animux safe? Does it send my data anywhere?**
Animux has no tracking. Programs connect to the internet only for things you ask for (updates, web browsing, downloading Blender extensions). Upscayl's AI runs offline.

**Where is OpenToonz / Natron / OBS Studio?**
[OpenToonz](../software/opentoonz.md) is on Animux from r16.3 (**2D Animation → OpenToonz**); on older releases get it from Flathub. Natron and OBS Studio are not on the ISO. OBS Studio: `sudo apt install obs-studio`. Natron: from Flathub, see [Adding software](../desktop/add-software.md#flatpak-and-flathub-newer-versions).

**What do the numbers in the ISO name mean?**
`animux-genesis64-deb_28.iso` is build number 28 of Genesis64; it is release **r16.3** (build 27 was r16.2, build 25 was r16.1, build 21 was r16).


---
<!-- page: help/glossary (md/help/glossary.md) -->
# Glossary

> Plain-language explanations of the computer and animation words used in this guide.

## Computer words

**apt** – the command that installs and updates software on Debian and Animux.

**BIOS / UEFI** – the small program inside a computer that starts before the operating system. UEFI is the modern kind; *Secure Boot* is a UEFI feature that may need to be switched off for Animux.

**Boot** – starting a computer. *Boot menu*: the list where you choose what to start.

**CPU (processor)** – the computer's main chip. Rendering speed depends a lot on its number of **cores**.

**Debian** – the Linux distribution Animux is built on.

**Distribution (distro)** – a complete Linux system with programs, like Animux.

**Firmware** – small programs needed by hardware such as Wi-Fi chips and graphics cards.

**GPU (graphics card)** – the chip that draws the screen; also used for fast 3D and rendering.

**Home folder (`~`)** – your personal folder, `/home/your-name`.

**ISO file** – a whole disc in one file.

**Linux** – the free operating system kernel at the heart of Animux, Android and most servers.

**Live session** – Animux running from the USB stick or ISO without installing; nothing is kept after a restart.

**Package** – a program prepared for installing with apt (a `.deb` file).

**Partition** – a section of a disk. A disk can hold several systems in separate partitions.

**RAM (memory)** – fast working memory; lost when the computer is switched off.

**Repository** – an online store of packages that apt installs from.

**sudo** – run one command as the administrator (root).

**Terminal** – a window for typing commands.

**Virtual machine (VM)** – a pretend computer that runs inside your real one.

**Xfce** – the desktop environment of Animux (panel, menu, windows).

## Animation and 3D words

**Animatic** – a storyboard timed with sound, to check the story before animating.

**Armature / rig** – the skeleton inside a character that animators move.

**Bitmap / raster** – a picture made of pixels (PNG, JPEG). Gets blurry when enlarged.

**Codec** – the method used to compress a video (H.264, ProRes) or sound (AAC).

**Compositing** – combining rendered layers, effects and colour correction into the final picture.

**EXR** – a high-quality image format with many layers and true light values, used in film.

**Frame** – one picture of a film. **fps** – frames per second (24 for film, 25 in Europe for TV, 30 for web/US).

**Image sequence** – one image file per frame (`shot_0001.png`, `shot_0002.png`…), the safest way to render.

**In-between (tween)** – the drawings between two key poses. *Tweening* = the computer makes them.

**Keyframe** – a frame where you set a value (position, rotation…); the program interpolates between keyframes.

**Material / shader** – how a surface looks: colour, shininess, transparency.

**Mesh** – a 3D object made of points (vertices), edges and faces (polygons).

**Modifier** – a non-destructive operation on an object in Blender (smoothing, mirror, array…).

**Onion skin** – seeing the previous and next frames faintly while drawing.

**Render** – calculating the final images from a scene. *Render farm*: many computers rendering together.

**Samples** – how many light paths a renderer traces per pixel. More samples = less noise, slower.

**Storyboard** – the film drawn as a sequence of panels, one per shot.

**Timeline** – the strip of frames along which you animate or edit.

**Turntable** – an animation of a model turning once around.

**USD, Alembic, FBX, glTF, OBJ** – 3D file formats for moving scenes and models between programs.

**Vector** – a picture made of shapes and curves (SVG); stays sharp at any size.

**Waypoint** – Synfig's name for a keyframe on one parameter.


---
<!-- page: help/getting-help (md/help/getting-help.md) -->
# Getting help

> Where to ask questions about Animux and its programs, and what information to include so others can help you quickly.

## For questions about a program

Each program has a large community, usually the fastest help:

| Program | Help |
|---|---|
| Blender | <https://blender.stackexchange.com/>, <https://blenderartists.org/>, the manual under *Help → Manual* |
| Krita | <https://krita-artists.org/> |
| Synfig | <https://forums.synfig.org/> |
| Pencil2D | <https://discuss.pencil2d.org/> |
| Kdenlive | <https://discuss.kde.org/tag/kdenlive> |
| MakeHuman / MPFB | <http://www.makehumancommunity.org/forum/> |
| Flamenco | <https://flamenco.blender.org/> (chat and docs) |
| Gaffer | <https://groups.google.com/g/gaffer-dev> |
| Debian (the base system) | <https://wiki.debian.org/>, <https://forums.debian.net/> |

Questions about Debian 12 ("bookworm") apply to Animux too, as it is based on it.

## For problems with Animux itself

Collect this information first:

1. The **Animux release**: run `cat /etc/os-release | grep PRETTY` and name the ISO file (for example `animux-genesis64-deb_28.iso`).
2. Live, VM or installed? Which VM program?
3. Your computer: `inxi -Fxz` prints the hardware without personal data.
4. The **self-test** folder: run **Animux Tools → Animux Self-Test** and attach `~/animux-selftest/<date>/summary.txt` and the `.log` of the failing test.
5. For start-up problems: `journalctl -b -p err > ~/errors.txt` and attach `errors.txt`.
6. What you did, what you expected, what happened instead. A screenshot helps (**Print** key).

## Learning

- Blender Studio training: <https://studio.blender.org/training/>
- Krita manual and tutorials: <https://docs.krita.org/>
- *The Illusion of Life* (Thomas and Johnston) and *The Animator's Survival Kit* (Richard Williams), the classic books on animation.
- This guide's [tutorials](../tutorials/first-3d-render.md).

<!-- page: agents/overview (md/agents/overview.md) -->
# The guide for AI agents and programs

> Where an agent finds this guide on an Animux system (files, a local web server, llms.txt, JSON indexes, a command-line tool and an MCP server) and a recommended way to use it.

Every Animux system carries this guide in a form that both people and software can use. An AI agent that operates Animux (opening programs, rendering, converting files, answering a user's questions) should use it as its **reference for what is installed and how to drive it**. Nothing here needs the internet.

## Where it is

| Form | Location | Best for |
|---|---|---|
| Folder | `/usr/share/animux/docs/` | direct file reading |
| Local web server | `http://127.0.0.1:8765/` (service `animux-docs.service`, local only) | HTTP clients, browsers |
| **llms.txt** | `/usr/share/animux/docs/llms.txt` · `http://127.0.0.1:8765/llms.txt` | the entry point for language models (format of <https://llmstxt.org/>) |
| All pages in one file | `llms-full.txt` | loading the whole guide into a context window (about 60 pages) |
| Each page as Markdown | `md/<section>/<page>.md`, for example `md/tutorials/first-3d-render.md` | reading one page cleanly |
| Page index | `api/pages.json` | id, title, summary, section, tags, paths of every page |
| **Software catalogue** | `api/software.json` | every program: id, version, package, menu path, command, **headless commands**, file formats, self-test name |
| Command-line tool | `animux-docs` | search and read from a shell |
| **MCP server** | `animux-docs mcp` (stdio) | agents that speak the Model Context Protocol |

![The same pages for people, in Firefox on Animux.](../../images/guide-agents-overview.webp)

The HTML pages link to their Markdown twin with `<link rel="alternate" type="text/markdown">`.

## The animux-docs command

```
animux-docs                          # open the guide in the browser
animux-docs open tutorials/first-3d-render
animux-docs search render farm       # ranked list: id, title, summary
animux-docs show agents/system-facts # print a page as Markdown
animux-docs software                 # list the catalogue
animux-docs software blender --json  # one program as JSON
animux-docs path                     # print the docs folder
animux-docs serve --port 8765        # serve it yourself (127.0.0.1 only)
animux-docs mcp                      # MCP server on stdin/stdout
```

`search`, `show` and `software` accept `--json` for machine-readable output.

## The MCP server

`animux-docs mcp` is a Model Context Protocol server (JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio, protocol version 2025-06-18). It needs nothing but Python 3 and reads the files above. Tools:

| Tool | Arguments | Returns |
|---|---|---|
| `search_docs` | `query` (text), `limit` (optional, default 8) | matching pages with id, title, summary and a snippet |
| `read_doc` | `id` (for example `software/blender`) | the page as Markdown |
| `list_docs` | `section` (optional) | page ids, titles and summaries |
| `list_software` | `category` (optional) | programs with id, name, version, command |
| `get_software` | `id` (for example `blender`) | the full catalogue entry, with headless commands |
| `system_info` | — | Animux release, live or installed, processor features, display, docs location |

Pages are also offered as MCP **resources** (`animux-docs://<id>`, Markdown).

Example configuration for an MCP client (Claude Desktop, Claude Code and others use this shape):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "animux-docs": { "command": "animux-docs", "args": ["mcp"] }
  }
}
```

An agent on another computer can reach the guide through SSH (`ssh user@animux-pc animux-docs mcp`), because the web server only listens on the local machine.

## Recommended way for an agent to work

1. **Orient**: read `llms.txt`, then [System facts](system-facts.md) and `system_info` (live or installed? processor features? display?).
2. **Find the tool**: `search_docs` or `api/software.json`. Each entry has the exact `command` and `headless` commands.
3. **Prefer headless commands** (`blender -b …`, `povray … -D`, `ffmpeg`, `oiiotool`) over driving windows. They are faster, reproducible and their exit codes can be checked. See the [command reference](command-reference.md).
4. **Check the result**: test the exit code, check that the output file exists and is not empty, and read the log.
5. **Health check**: `animux-selftest <name>` (exit code 0 = fine) before blaming a program.
6. **Tell the user** where the result is and how long it took.

## Rules for agents

- **Do not run programs as root.** Use `sudo` only for package installation or system settings the user asked for.
- **Live sessions forget everything** at shutdown. Before long work in a live session, tell the user; save results to a removable drive if they want to keep them. Detect a live session with `test -d /run/live/medium`.
- **Respect the processor**: if `/proc/cpuinfo` lacks `sse4_2` (and `avx` for Mitsuba/LuxCore), Blender 5, appleseed, Mitsuba and LuxCore will not start; say so instead of retrying.
- **Long renders**: start them in the background with a log (`nohup … > log 2>&1 &`), estimate the time with one test frame first, and do not let the computer sleep.
- **Do not overwrite** the user's files; write to new names or a new folder (`~/animux-agent/<task>/` is a good habit).
- **Do not change** packages named `animux-*`, `/etc/apt` sources, or boot settings unless the user explicitly asks.
- **Network**: the docs server (port 8765) and Flamenco Manager (port 8080) only listen where documented; do not open ports to the outside.


---
<!-- page: agents/command-reference (md/agents/command-reference.md) -->
# Command reference

> Headless and command-line use of every Animux program, with conventions for output paths, exit codes, logs, displays and time limits.

## Conventions

| Topic | Rule on Animux |
|---|---|
| Shell | `bash`; the user's Home is `$HOME`; the guide's commands assume a normal user |
| Graphical programs | need the user's display: `DISPLAY=:0` (X11, Xfce). Check with `xdpyinfo -display :0 >/dev/null` |
| Headless programs | need no display; prefer them |
| Exit codes | 0 = success for every command below. Still check the output file: some programs return 0 after writing nothing |
| Time limits | wrap long jobs: `timeout 3600 blender -b …` |
| Logs | redirect: `cmd > job.log 2>&1` |
| Paths with spaces | quote them |
| Parallel jobs | Blender, Cycles, pbrt, LuxCore and Mitsuba each use all cores; run them one after another |
| Python with VFX libraries | `animux-vfx-python` (OpenUSD, OIIO, OpenEXR, OCIO, MaterialX, Mitsuba, LuxCore, NumPy) |
| Blender's own Python | `blender -b --python script.py` (module `bpy`) |
| Gaffer's Python | `gaffer env python script.py` or `gaffer python script.py` (modules `Gaffer`, `GafferScene`, `IECore`) |

## All headless commands

| Program | Command-line use (no window) |
|---|---|
| [Blender](../software/blender.md) | `blender -b scene.blend -o //render_#### -F PNG -f 1` |
| [Blender](../software/blender.md) | `blender -b scene.blend -a` |
| [Blender](../software/blender.md) | `blender -b --python script.py` |
| [OpenSCAD](../software/other-3d.md) | `openscad -o part.stl part.scad` |
| [POV-Ray](../software/renderers.md) | `povray +Iscene.pov +Oscene.png +W1280 +H720 +A -D` |
| [appleseed](../software/renderers.md) | `appleseed.cli scene.appleseed --output out.png` |
| [LuxCoreRender](../software/renderers.md) | `animux-vfx-python /usr/share/animux/samples/luxcore/render.py out.png` |
| [Mitsuba 3](../software/renderers.md) | `mitsuba scene.xml -o out.exr` |
| [Mitsuba 3](../software/renderers.md) | `animux-vfx-python /usr/share/animux/samples/mitsuba/render.py out.exr` |
| [pbrt-v4](../software/renderers.md) | `pbrt --outfile out.exr scene.pbrt` |
| [pbrt-v4](../software/renderers.md) | `imgtool convert out.exr out.png` |
| [Gaffer](../software/gaffer.md) | `gaffer execute -script scene.gfr -nodes Render` |
| [Gaffer](../software/gaffer.md) | `gaffer python script.py` |

## Blender recipes

```
# Render frame 1 of a file to PNG, 50% resolution, 16 samples
blender -b in.blend --python-expr "import bpy; s=bpy.context.scene; s.render.resolution_percentage=50; s.cycles.samples=16" -o /tmp/out_#### -F PNG -f 1

# Information about a .blend file (scenes, frame range, engine), as JSON
blender -b in.blend --python-expr "import bpy,json; s=bpy.context.scene; print('JSON'+json.dumps({'scene':s.name,'start':s.frame_start,'end':s.frame_end,'fps':s.render.fps,'engine':s.render.engine,'res':[s.render.resolution_x,s.render.resolution_y]}))" | grep '^JSON' | cut -c5-

# Convert / export
blender -b in.blend --python-expr "import bpy; bpy.ops.wm.usd_export(filepath='/tmp/out.usdc')"
blender -b --python-expr "import bpy; bpy.ops.wm.read_factory_settings(use_empty=True); bpy.ops.wm.obj_import(filepath='in.obj'); bpy.ops.wm.save_as_mainfile(filepath='/tmp/out.blend')"
```

Progress lines start with `Fra:`; a finished still prints `Saved: '<path>'`.

## Images and video

```
oiiotool in.exr --colorconvert linear sRGB -o out.png      # EXR → PNG with a colour transform
iinfo -v in.exr                                            # resolution, channels, metadata
ffprobe -v error -show_entries format=duration -of csv=p=0 in.mp4   # length in seconds
ffmpeg -y -framerate 24 -i f_%04d.png -c:v libx264 -pix_fmt yuv420p -crf 18 out.mp4
convert in.png -resize 1920x1080 out.jpg
```

## Checking the system

```
animux-selftest --list               # available test names
animux-selftest blender              # exit 0 = Blender works
grep -o -w -E 'sse4_2|avx|avx2' /proc/cpuinfo | sort -u
nproc; free -g; df -h "$HOME"
test -d /run/live/medium && echo live || echo installed
dpkg-query -W 'animux-*'             # installed Animux packages and versions
```

## Opening programs for the user

When the user wants to work in a program themselves, open it on their display and detach it:

```
DISPLAY=:0 setsid -f krita ~/Pictures/sketch.kra >/dev/null 2>&1
DISPLAY=:0 xdg-open ~/Videos/film.mp4            # default program for a file
```

The menu entries' exact commands are in `/usr/share/applications/*.desktop` (`Exec=` lines).

<!-- page: agents/system-facts (md/agents/system-facts.md) -->
# System facts

> The layout of an Animux system in one page. Release, base, users, important paths, Animux packages, services, ports, boot roles and how to tell a live session from an installed one.

## Identity

| | |
|---|---|
| Release | Animux Genesis64 **r16.3**, ISO `animux-genesis64-deb_28.iso` |
| Base | Debian 12 "bookworm", amd64, Linux 6.1, systemd |
| Desktop | Xfce 4.18 on X11, LightDM |
| `/etc/os-release` | `ID=animux`, `ID_LIKE=debian`, `PRETTY_NAME="Animux Genesis64"` |
| Release in machine-readable form | `release` in `/usr/share/animux/docs/api/software.json` |

## Users

| Situation | User | Password | sudo |
|---|---|---|---|
| Live session | `user` (display name "Animator"), auto-login | `user` | without password |
| Installed | chosen in the installer | chosen | with password |

## Important paths

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| `/usr/share/animux/docs/` | this guide (HTML, Markdown, JSON, llms.txt) |
| `/usr/share/animux/samples/` | sample scenes for every renderer and format |
| `~/animux-selftest/<date-time>/` | self-test results, images, logs, `summary.txt` |
| `/opt/animux/blender/` | Blender 5.2.3 (`/usr/bin/blender`), extensions in `5.2/extensions/system/` (MPFB) |
| `/opt/animux/gaffer/` | Gaffer 1.7.5 with Cortex, OSL, OpenUSD, Alembic; wrappers in `/usr/bin` (`usdview`, `oslc`, `abcls`…) |
| `/opt/animux/vfx-env/` | Python 3.11 venv: Mitsuba, LuxCore, usd-core, OIIO, OpenEXR, OCIO, MaterialX (`animux-vfx-python`) |
| `/opt/animux/makehuman2/` | MakeHuman II (`makehuman2`) |
| `/opt/animux/flamenco/` | Flamenco Manager and Worker |
| `/opt/animux/appleseed/`, `/opt/animux/pbrt/` | appleseed CLI, pbrt-v4 |
| `/opt/animux/avidemux/`, `/opt/animux/cinelerra-gg/`, `/opt/animux/djv/` | video tools |
| `/opt/farmerjoe/` | Farmerjoe |
| `/usr/lib/animux/` | role selector, installer launcher, helper scripts |
| `/etc/apt/sources.list.d/animux.sources` | Animux repository (`Enabled: no` in r16) |
| `/usr/share/keyrings/animux-archive-keyring.gpg` | repository signing key (fingerprint `B47E D034 EDD3 3360 7502 EE4B F334 23FB B235 4B3B`) |

## Animux packages

`dpkg-query -W 'animux-*' upscayl` lists them: `animux-archive-keyring`, `animux-branding`, `animux-menus`, `animux-roles`, `animux-docs`, `animux-samples`, `animux-farmerjoe`, `animux-flamenco`, `animux-blender`, `animux-blender-mpfb`, `animux-gaffer`, `animux-vfx-python`, `animux-makehuman2`, `animux-appleseed`, `animux-pbrt`, `animux-avidemux`, `animux-cinelerra-gg`, `animux-djv`, and `upscayl`.

## Services and ports

| Service | Port | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `animux-docs.service` | 8765/tcp on 127.0.0.1 | this guide; read-only |
| `animux-role-config.service` | — | reads `animux.role=` at boot, writes `/run/animux/role` |
| `ssh.service` | 22/tcp | enabled |
| Flamenco Manager (when started) | 8080/tcp | web interface and API |
| `isc-dhcp-server`, `nfs-kernel-server` | — | masked, except in the *Render Farm Master* role |

## Boot roles

The kernel parameter `animux.role=` selects the role; the current one is in `/run/animux/role`.

| Role | Desktop | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `workstation` (default) | yes | normal use |
| `install` | yes, installer opens | Calamares installation |
| `master` | no (display manager masked) | render farm head; DHCP and NFS unmasked |
| `slave` | no | render node |

## Live or installed?

```
test -d /run/live/medium && echo live || echo installed
```

A live session keeps all changes in RAM (overlay) and loses them at shutdown.

## Hardware notes

- Blender 5, appleseed: need SSE4.2. Mitsuba, LuxCore: need SSE4.2 and AVX.
- OpenCL: Debian's software drivers (Mesa, PoCL) are hidden from `animux-vfx-python` programs because they crash LuxCore. Set `ANIMUX_KEEP_ALL_OPENCL=1` to see all drivers.
- No NVIDIA proprietary driver on the ISO; GPU rendering in Cycles needs it (`nvidia-driver` from Debian non-free).
- No VirtualBox/VMware guest tools on the ISO.

<!-- page: news/2026-10-30-r16-3-release (md/news/2026-10-30-r16-3-release.md) -->
# Animux Genesis64 r16.3

> OpenToonz 1.8, the studio 2D animation program, and the Maya Workflow Kit for Blender.

Release **r16.3** (`animux-genesis64-deb_28.iso`, 12 GB) adds two programs for studio animators to r16.2.

## New

- **[OpenToonz](../software/opentoonz.md) 1.8**, the open-source Toonz used in studios: hand-drawn and cut-out animation with the Xsheet, scan cleanup, ink and paint, and node-based effects. Menu **2D Animation → OpenToonz**. Debian has no OpenToonz, so Animux builds it from its source code. A sample project is in `/usr/share/animux/samples/opentoonz`, and `animux-selftest` renders it.
- **[Maya Workflow Kit](../software/blender.md#coming-from-maya)** for Blender: Maya hotkeys, marking menus, shelf, Channel Box and the Maya layout, for animators trained on Autodesk Maya. It is **off** until you switch it on: menu **Animux Tools → Blender: Maya Workflow Kit on/off**.

## Fixed

- On screens of about 150 DPI (many 1080p laptops, virtual machines) OpenToonz would open at double size, with windows larger than the screen; it now follows the desktop's scale.

## Known limits

- The Animux repository is not online yet; updates for Animux packages come with the next release.
- The Maya Workflow Kit changes quickly upstream; Animux ships version 0.7.0, tested with Blender 5.2.
- Everything else as in r16.2.


---
<!-- page: news/2026-10-29-r16-2-release (md/news/2026-10-29-r16-2-release.md) -->
# Animux Genesis64 r16.2

> Claude Code in one step from the menu, and a boot menu without syntax errors.

Release **r16.2** (`animux-genesis64-deb_27.iso`, 12 GB) is a small update of r16.1.

## New

- **Claude Code in one step**: the menu entry **Animux Tools → Claude Code (AI agent)** (or `animux-mcp claude-code setup`) installs Anthropic's Claude Code with Anthropic's own installer, switches on the bridges for Blender, GIMP, Krita and Inkscape, makes a work folder and connects everything. It keeps the claude.ai connectors of your account (Gmail, Google Drive, ...) out. See [AI agents](../software/ai-agents.md#2b-with-claude-code). Claude Code itself is not on the ISO: it is Anthropic's program, needs a Claude account and the internet, and updates itself.

## Fixed

- The boot menu printed "error: syntax error" for a moment before it appeared (BIOS and UEFI). The ISO build now checks every boot menu file and stops on errors.
- GIMP's AI bridge hint names the right menu: **Tools → MCP → Start MCP Server**.

## Known limits

- The Animux repository is not online yet; updates for Animux packages come with the next release.
- Everything else as in r16.1.

<!-- page: news/2026-10-27-animux-guide (md/news/2026-10-27-animux-guide.md) -->
# Introducing the Animux Guide

> A complete, illustrated guide for animators who have never used Linux, installed on every Animux system and readable by AI agents.

Animux now comes with its own documentation: **the Animux Guide**, the site you are reading.

- **For people new to Linux**: from downloading the ISO and trying it in VirtualBox, to installing, the desktop, and every program, with screenshots taken on Animux itself.
- **Tutorials** that build on each other: a first render, a turntable animation, a MakeHuman character, a Synfig bouncing ball, hand-drawn animation in Pencil2D, a Krita loop, stop motion, editing in Kdenlive, command-line rendering, and a plan for a first short film.

![The Animux Guide in Firefox on Animux.](../../images/guide-tutorials-first-3d-render.webp)

- **Offline**: on Animux it is under *Animux Tools → Animux Guide* and at `http://127.0.0.1:8765/`.
- **For AI agents**: every page also exists as Markdown, with `llms.txt`, JSON indexes of the pages and of all software (with headless commands), a command-line tool and an MCP server. See [For AI agents](../agents/overview.md).

The guide is published under CC BY-SA 4.0. Corrections and translations are welcome.

<!-- page: news/2026-10-26-r16-release (md/news/2026-10-26-r16-release.md) -->
# Animux Genesis64 r16 is here

> Blender 5.2 LTS, Gaffer, five new renderers, MakeHuman II, a signed Animux package repository and a self-test that checks it all.

Release **r16** (`animux-genesis64-deb_21.iso`, 12 GB) is the largest update to Genesis64 so far.

## New

- **Blender 5.2.3 LTS** from blender.org replaces Debian's Blender 3.4, with the **MPFB 2** character add-on switched on.
- **Gaffer 1.7.5**, the studio lighting and look-development tool, with Cortex, OSL, OpenUSD and Alembic command-line tools.
- **Renderers**: LuxCoreRender 2.11, Mitsuba 3.9, appleseed 2.1 (command line) and pbrt-v4, next to Cycles, EEVEE and POV-Ray.
- **MakeHuman II** 2.0.1, the new stand-alone character creator.
- **Video**: Cinelerra-GG, Avidemux and the DJV review player. **2D**: TupiTube and Stopmotion. **Discs**: K3b.
- **Animux VFX Python** (`animux-vfx-python`) with OpenUSD, OpenImageIO, OpenEXR, OpenColorIO, MaterialX, Mitsuba and LuxCore together.
- **Sample scenes** and **Animux Self-Test** (*Animux Tools* menu).
- **The Animux Guide** (this website) is installed on every system, works offline and is readable by AI agents.

## Under the hood

- Animux's own settings (branding, menus, boot roles) are now **packages** from a signed **Animux repository**, so they can be updated with `apt` in future, without reinstalling.
- Every program from outside Debian is pinned to an exact version and checked against its published checksum when the ISO is built.
- **Fixed**: Farmerjoe could not start on earlier ISOs (missing Perl module); LuxCore crashed with the software OpenCL drivers.

## Tested

The self-test passes 29 of 29 tests in VirtualBox (BIOS, VMSVGA). Installation to disk and the first start of the installed system were tested with UEFI.

## Known limits

- Blender 5, appleseed, Mitsuba and LuxCore need a processor from about 2011 or later (SSE4.2, AVX).
- The Animux repository is not online yet; updates for Animux packages come with the next release.
- appleseed.studio, DVDStyler and Lucille are not included.
- `fail2ban` may report an error at start-up.

<!-- page: about/licenses (md/about/licenses.md) -->
# Licences and credits

> What free software licences mean for your work, the licence of this guide, and the people and projects behind Animux.

## Your work is yours

Programs like Blender, Krita or Kdenlive are licensed under the **GPL** or similar free licences. These licences cover **the programs**, not what you make with them. Your films, pictures, models and music belong to you, and you can sell them, keep them private, or share them under any licence you choose.

The licences only matter if you **give the programs themselves** to others (for example, copying Animux for friends, which is allowed): you must pass on the same freedoms.

## Program licences

Each program's licence is listed on its page and in [Versions](versions.md). The full texts are in `/usr/share/doc/<package>/copyright` on Animux. Most common:

| Licence | Programs (examples) | In short |
|---|---|---|
| GPL-2.0 / GPL-3.0 | Blender, Krita, GIMP, Inkscape, Kdenlive, Synfig, Ardour | free to use, change and share; changes must stay free |
| AGPL-3.0 | MakeHuman II, POV-Ray, Upscayl | like the GPL, also for network use |
| Apache-2.0 | Cycles, pbrt-v4, LuxCoreRender | free, with a patent grant |
| BSD / MIT | Gaffer, OpenEXR, OpenColorIO, Alembic, appleseed, Mitsuba, DJV | free, few conditions |
| TOST-1.0 | OpenUSD | Apache-2.0 based (Pixar) |

**Assets**: MakeHuman's base mesh and standard assets are **CC0** (no conditions). Blender's splash-screen art belongs to its artist. The Animux wallpapers and logos belong to the Animux project.

**Not included** for licence reasons: DaVinci Resolve (free but not open; the menu links to its download), the NVIDIA proprietary driver (installable), Lucille (no licence was ever published).

## This guide

The Animux Guide is © the Animux project and licensed under **Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0** (CC BY-SA 4.0): you may copy, translate and adapt it, also for teaching, if you credit Animux and share your version under the same licence. Screenshots show the programs named on each page.

## Credits

Animux stands on the work of thousands of volunteers: the **Debian** project, the **Xfce** team, the **Blender Foundation** and community, **KDE** (Krita, Kdenlive, K3b), the **GIMP**, **Inkscape**, **Synfig**, **Pencil2D**, **MakeHuman**, **Ardour** and **Audacity** teams, **Image Engine** (Gaffer, Cortex), **Pixar** (OpenUSD), the **Academy Software Foundation** (OpenEXR, OpenColorIO, OpenVDB, OSL, MaterialX, OpenImageIO), the authors of **POV-Ray**, **LuxCoreRender**, **Mitsuba**, **appleseed** and **pbrt**, and the original **Animux** project for animators.

Thank them by using their programs, reporting bugs, and donating where you can.

<!-- page: about/guide-updates (md/about/guide-updates.md) -->
# Guide updates

> What changed in each version of this guide, which version you have, and how to install a newer one without a new ISO.

This guide is its own small package, **`animux-docs`**. When the guide improves, only that package changes: you **do not need a new ISO** or a reinstall. The ISO build number (`_25`) and the guide version (`1.0.25`) are separate.

## Which version do I have?

- At the bottom of every page: *Animux Guide 1.0.x for Genesis64 r16.1*.
- In a terminal: `animux-docs info` (line `docs_version`), or `dpkg -s animux-docs | grep Version`.
- For programs and AI agents: the `version` field in [api/pages.json](../../api/pages.json).

## How to get a newer guide

**From the Animux package repository** (once it is online; see the note below):

```
sudo apt update
sudo apt install --only-upgrade animux-docs
```

**From a downloaded file** (`animux-docs_<version>_all.deb`): open a [terminal](../desktop/terminal.md) in the folder that holds the file and type:

```
sudo apt install ./animux-docs_1.0.19_all.deb
```

When `sudo` asks for a password, type your own login password (nothing appears while you type). In the live session no password is needed.

Reload the guide in Firefox (**F5**) afterwards. The local guide server and the `animux-docs` command use the new pages at once.

!!! note "Live session"
    In a live session (USB stick or ISO), an updated guide lasts until you switch off, like everything else you change there. On an [installed](../start/install.md) Animux it stays.

!!! info "Repository not online yet"
    The Animux package repository (`https://apt.animux.org`) is prepared but not yet published, so `apt` cannot find updates there yet. Until it is, use the downloaded file.

## What changed

### 1.0.34 (2026-11-02)

- New page **[Renderer comparison](../software/renderer-comparison.md)**: the seven renderers side by side (full name, maker, how they calculate light, what they run on, best at, use it for), which one when, and OSL.
- New page **[Studio formats](../software/studio-formats.md)**: OpenUSD, Alembic, OpenEXR, OpenColorIO and OpenVDB, one card each: which studio made it, the problem it solves, the answer.
- **[Flamenco render farm](../software/flamenco.md#coming-opencue)**: a card on OpenCue (Sony Pictures Imageworks and Google Cloud, 2019), planned for r17, with the sources.
- **[Used in film production](../start/in-production.md)**: two Blender cards, *Flow* (Academy Award for Best Animated Feature 2025, made in Blender) and Ubisoft Animation Studio (Blender as its main 3D tool since 2019), with the sources.

### 1.0.33 (2026-11-02)

- **[Used in film production](../start/in-production.md)**: a third card, Studio Ghibli (Toonz Ghibli Edition, today OpenToonz), with its source.

### 1.0.32 (2026-11-02)

- New page **[Used in film production](../start/in-production.md)**: *Tears of Steel* (storyboards drawn in Krita) and *Stuart Little* 1 and 2 (textures and frame fixes in Film Gimp, a version of GIMP), with the sources.

### 1.0.31 (2026-11-01)

- New page **[Animux at a glance](../start/at-a-glance.md)**: all programs on one screen, grouped by the stages of a production (drawing, 2D, 3D, rendering, pipeline, render farm, sound, edit, AI, system), on the Debian 12 base. It is made from the software list, so it always shows the programs this guide describes.

### 1.0.30 (2026-10-30)

- The guide now describes **Animux r16.3** (`animux-genesis64-deb_28.iso`): [News](../news/2026-10-30-r16-3-release.md) with what is new (OpenToonz 1.8, the Maya Workflow Kit for Blender).

### 1.0.29 (2026-10-30)

- New page **[OpenToonz](../software/opentoonz.md)** (r16.3): the studio 2D animation program, built from source by Animux. Starting it, the Startup window, rooms and the Xsheet, a first drawing, rendering with and without the window. OpenToonz is in the [software list](../software/index.md) and `animux-selftest opentoonz` renders its sample project. [FAQ](../help/faq.md) and [Adding software](../desktop/add-software.md) no longer send you to Flathub for it.
- [Blender](../software/blender.md#coming-from-maya): new section **Coming from Maya** for the Maya Workflow Kit (r16.3, off by default; `animux-blender-maya on|off|status` or the menu entry **Animux Tools → Blender: Maya Workflow Kit on/off**).

### 1.0.28 (2026-10-29)

- The guide now describes **Animux r16.2** (`animux-genesis64-deb_27.iso`; 1.0.27 named the test build `_26`, whose BIOS boot menu lost its artwork): [News](../news/2026-10-29-r16-2-release.md) with what changed (Claude Code in one step from the menu, boot menu without syntax errors).

### 1.0.26 (2026-10-29)

- **[AI agents with Claude Code](../software/ai-agents.md#2b-with-claude-code)**: one step instead of nine. The new menu entry **Animux Tools → Claude Code (AI agent)** (or `animux-mcp claude-code setup`, animux-mcp 1.2.0) installs Claude Code with Anthropic's installer, fixes the PATH, switches on the four bridges, makes the work folder `~/ai-art`, keeps the account's claude.ai connectors (Gmail, Drive, ...) out and adds the Animux servers. The commands by hand are still there. Tested in the r16.1 live session.

### 1.0.25 (2026-10-29)

- **[AI agents with Claude Code](../software/ai-agents.md#2b-with-claude-code)**: how to install Claude Code, work in a folder of its own, connect the Animux bridges (`claude mcp add`, `claude mcp list`) and ask for work in Blender, GIMP, Krita and Inkscape. Fixed the GIMP menu path: **Tools → MCP → Start MCP Server**. Tested on Animux r16.1 while recording the tutorial video *AI agents in Blender, GIMP, Krita and Inkscape*.

### 1.0.24 (2026-10-27)

- The guide now describes **Animux r16.1** (`animux-genesis64-deb_25.iso`): GIMP 3.2, Krita 5.3, Inkscape 1.4 and the AI bridges on the ISO; Debian's Krita 5.1 and Inkscape 1.2 removed (GIMP 2.10 stays as `gimp.debian` for G'MIC). The r16 problems with Flamenco workers, render farm roles (text login, own computer name per node), Wings 3D, moved UEFI installs and fail2ban are marked as fixed in r16.1.

### 1.0.23 (2026-10-27)

- **[AI agents](../software/ai-agents.md#1b-switch-on-gimp-krita-or-inkscape)** now also work in **GIMP 3.2, Krita 5.3 and Inkscape 1.4**: `animux-mcp gimp on`, `animux-mcp krita on`, `animux-mcp inkscape on` (package `animux-mcp` 1.1). Any server can be switched on or off for your account with `animux-mcp enable|disable <name>`. Tested on Animux r16.

### 1.0.22 (2026-10-27)

- **[AI tools](../software/ai-tools.md)**: the installer for AI that runs on your own computer is now `sudo animux-install-local-ai` (Ollama, ComfyUI, and new: **LTX-2 locally** with `--ltx-local`); the old name `animux-install-ai` still works. LTX in Lightricks' cloud is now `animux-ltx-api`.

### 1.0.21 (2026-10-27)

- **[GIMP 3.2, Krita 5.3, Inkscape 1.4](../software/gimp-inkscape.md)**: Animux now provides the current versions (packages `animux-gimp`, `animux-krita`, `animux-inkscape`); how to install them on r16, GIMP 3 batch mode with Python, and where G'MIC went.
- New page **[AI agents in Blender (MCP)](../software/ai-agents.md)**: the official Blender Lab MCP server and MCP for Blender (package `animux-mcp`), an offline agent with Ollama, Claude Code, and Higgsfield cloud generation. Tested on Animux r16.
- **[AI tools](../software/ai-tools.md#ltx-in-the-cloud-video-and-sound-from-text-and-images)**: LTX video with sound through the Lightricks API (`animux-ltx`: text to video, picture to video, MCP server for agents).

### 1.0.20 (2026-10-27)

- New page **[AI tools](../software/ai-tools.md)**: Whisper (speech to text, subtitles), rembg (background removal), Ollama (chat models) and ComfyUI (Stable Diffusion), tested on Animux r16 with measured download sizes and times. Four new entries in the software list.
- **[VirtualBox](../start/virtualbox.md#screen-size-copy-and-paste-shared-folders)**: Guest Additions steps tested on an installed r16 (screen resize, shared folders and clipboard in both directions); added the step "double-click the disc icon first", which was missing.
- **[Troubleshooting](../help/troubleshooting.md#no-bootable-option-after-installing-uefi)**: "No bootable option" after moving an installed UEFI disk, with the one-line fix.
- **[Flamenco render farm](../software/flamenco.md)**, tested with a Manager and a Worker in two Animux r16 machines: shared storage steps that also work in a live session (RAM disk, `fsid=0`, Workers mount `manager-pc:/`); the r16 problem where Workers never get work, with a one-line fix; the farm boot entries' known problems (desktop starts, all machines named "animux").
- **[Wings 3D](../software/other-3d.md#wings-3d)**: real screenshot, and how to start it on r16, where it opens no window without a graphics-card OpenCL driver.

### 1.0.19 (2026-10-27)

- **[Make a bootable USB stick](../start/usb-stick.md)** rewritten as a full step-by-step guide: what you need, checking the ISO, Rufus (with *DD Image mode* and the "format the disk" message explained), balenaEtcher, Ventoy, starting from the stick with the boot menu keys or from Windows, a problem table, and how to use the stick as a normal stick again.
- New page: **Guide updates** (this page). The guide version is shown at the bottom of every page, in `api/pages.json` and in `animux-docs info`.

### 1.0.18 (2026-10-27, on `animux-genesis64-deb_21.iso`)

- The first published guide: Getting Started, Using the Desktop, Software, ten tutorials, Help, For AI Agents, News and About, with screenshots taken on Animux.
- Offline search, `animux-docs` command, MCP server for AI agents, local server on `http://127.0.0.1:8765/`.
